KEY MESSAGE 1...Isolated shower possible today, but drier overall. 
Dry Thursday with seasonably cool temperatures.

Low pressure centered over central NY will continue to track east 
into northern New England through the day today. With this passing 
low, its trailing cold front will cross over southern New England 
and high pressure will build in slowly behind it. Skies are expected 
to steadily clear through the day today as a result. An isolated 
shower cannot be ruled out this afternoon given the passage of this 
disturbance, and latest CAMs did hint at a low chance for an 
isolated shower or two to develop.

Latest model soundings continue to indicate decent mixing during the 
day today, which will lend itself to gusty W winds up to 20-30 mph, 
though locally higher gusts in the higher terrain cannot be ruled 
out. With these aforementioned gusty westerly winds, downsloping 
flow is anticipated today which will combine with warmer 
temperatures aloft to support a much warmer fall day. 925 mb 
temperatures are expected to range between 16-18C, with the southern 
coastal areas possibly reaching 20C aloft. Though temperatures are 
not expected to hit 80F, highs in the 70s today will overspread 
southern New England, and some spots in the southern CT River Valley 
and SE MA could get very close to 80F. Despite these warmer 
temperatures, dew points will remain comfortably in the 50s and 60s.

Heading into tonight and Thursday, high pressure strongly takes hold 
of the region along with a significantly drier airmass. PWATs fall 
to as low as 0.2" and winds slacken considerably, becoming light to 
calm. The warmer airmass overhead today shifts off to the east and 
is replaced by a notably cooler one with 925 mb temperatures falling 
below 10C. This will be supportive of cooler lows tonight and a 
cooler day Thursday: lows will fall into the 40s and low 50s, and 
highs Thursday will top out in the low 60s.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Low pressure system expected to bring rain Friday 
into early Saturday. Gusty NW winds and below normal temperatures 
expected to be left in its wake.

A strong northern stream shortwave trough is expected to shift 
across the Great Lakes and into the northeast Friday into Saturday. 
The overall consensus across the deterministic and ensemble guidance 
is that the surface low sets up across western NY and southeastern 
Ontario by Friday morning, with rain moving into southern New 
England at this same time. An upper level jet sets up near southern 
New England (at 250 mb over the region, this jet may reach around 
120-150 kt based on latest guidance), providing support for broad 
synoptic ascent. With this setup, an anomalous moisture plume will 
be advected in from the SW. NAEFS guidance has PWAT values 
approaching 3 standard deviations above normal over the region by 
Friday morning, and IVT values reaching the maximum of the CFSR 
climatology by early Friday afternoon. Notably, too, temperatures 
aloft with this plume are quite warm, with 925 mb temperatures 
briefly returning to around 16-18C and 850 mb temperatures to around 
10C. Ensemble guidance has a bit more agreement this morning 
regarding rainfall totals, generally ranging between 0.4-0.7". 
Across all ensembles, some higher probabilities of totals reaching 
or exceeding 1.0" exist over parts of central and western MA, 
especially towards the Berkshires. Mean totals also trend slightly 
higher there across guidance, generally getting to just under an 
inch. Deterministic guidance indicates some signal for lines of more 
convective showers, but details regarding how much may fall within 
those and where they set up are still uncertain at this time.

Aside from the upper level jet, a southerly LLJ is slated to set up 
over the region Friday, with values at 925 mb ranging between 40-50 
kt at its maximum. If mixed well, we could see some breezy or gusty 
SW winds. Gusts could range between 25-35 mph, with higher gusts 
possible for the Cape and Islands, especially as the core of this 
jet sets up over these areas.

Following this rainfall, a strong cold front is expected to push 
through the region Saturday morning, kicking off strong cold air 
advection underneath more cyclonic flow. Latest guidance indicates 
925 mb temperatures sinking below 0C Saturday as this pattern kicks 
off. PWATs fall below 0.25" once more as this dry, cold air sets in. 
Lows Friday night fall into the 40s and upper 30s, with the higher 
elevations likely falling below to at freezing. Highs Saturday may 
struggle to reach the low 50s across the interior and lows Saturday 
night will likely dip below freezing across the region based on the 
latest ensemble probabilities, with the exceptions being areas 
closest to the coasts and urban areas. Though, those areas will
